.. _reference-linked-papi:

====================
Linking a PAPI Build
====================

For cyPAPI to be successfully installed you need to link with a PAPI build
that has your desired components configured in.

Downloading PAPI
================

To download a copy of PAPI you can clone it from the GitHub repository:

.. code-block:: console

   $ git clone https://github.com/icl-utk-edu/papi.git

Configuring and Installing PAPI
===============================

After successfully downloading PAPI, we must now configure and install.

To configure PAPI with just the CPU components:

.. code-block:: console

   $ ./configure --prefix=$PWD/test-install

To configure PAPI with various components:

.. code-block:: console

   $ ./configure --prefix=$PWD/test-install --with-components="cuda ..."

To see an exhaustive list of supported components please see the table in the section titled `List of Components`_.

.. _List of components: https://github.com/icl-utk-edu/papi/wiki/PAPI-Overview#list-of-components

After configuring PAPI with the options and components desired, run:

.. code-block:: console

    $ make && make install

Verify your PAPI Build was Successful
=====================================

Once the compliation has been completed, verify that the components you configured in are active by running ``papi_component_avail``:

.. code-block:: console

    $ cd test-install/bin
    $ ./papi_component_avail

As an example, configuring PAPI with just the CPU components with the correct permissions would net the following truncated output from ``papi_component_avail``:

.. code-block:: console

    --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Compiled-in components:
    Name:   perf_event              Linux perf_event CPU counters
    Name:   perf_event_uncore       Linux perf_event CPU uncore and northbridge
    Name:   sysdetect               System info detection component

    Active components:
    Name:   perf_event              Linux perf_event CPU counters
                                    Native: 176, Preset: 59, Counters: 10
                                    PMUs supported: ix86arch, perf, perf_raw, skx

    Name:   perf_event_uncore       Linux perf_event CPU uncore and northbridge
                                    Native: 2867, Preset: 0, Counters: 168
                                    PMUs supported: rapl, skx_unc_cha0, skx_unc_cha1, skx_unc_cha2, skx_unc_cha3, skx_unc_cha4
                                                    skx_unc_cha5, skx_unc_cha6, skx_unc_cha7, skx_unc_cha8, skx_unc_cha9

                                    Native: 0, Preset: 0, Counters: 0


    -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

Export PAPI_DIR
===============

As cyPAPI is an intermediate Python interface to access PAPI profiling features, one must export the environment variable ``PAPI_DIR``.
This environment variable needs to be assigned to your PAPI build install path, as an example:

.. code-block:: console

   $ export PAPI_DIR=$PWD/test-install

After this has been done, you can now build cyPAPI.
